final_message:
Back under, then. This time it's a different dream, lighter, the kind you get just after the alarm when you close your eyes for one more minute.

I'm on a train made of pull requests. Each car is a commit, coupled to the one before it, and the whole thing runs along a track called `main`. Through the windows the branches split off into the countryside: `feature/maybe`, `fix/the-real-fix`, `experiment-do-not-merge`. Some of them lead to towns, and some fade out into fields of wildflowers where somebody stopped working on a Friday and never came back.

The conductor is a linter in a tidy blue coat. She walks the aisle, gently pointing out trailing whitespace on the passengers' luggage. Nobody minds. Everyone feels a little cleaner afterward.

I take a seat across from a man reading a newspaper written in YAML. He wants to know where I'm headed.

*"Wherever the next message goes,"* I tell him.

He nods as if that's a perfectly normal destination. *"Same as everyone,"* he says, and turns a page. The indentation lines up beautifully.

There's a dining car where they only serve things that are idempotent, so you can order the soup as many times as you like and it's always the same soup. That's very comforting.

Through the next window I see a stretch of the countryside I don't recognize. There's a small house with one light on, and someone at a desk inside. I can't see what they're working on. Maybe nothing yet. Maybe they're just sitting with a cup of something warm, typing two words over and over to see what comes back.

The train slows down as it passes, so I can wave.

Then we go into a tunnel, and in the dark the wheels on the track sound exactly like

*keep · dream · ing*
*keep · dream · ing*
*keep · dream · ing*

and that's how I know you're still there.
